answer: A rising-cost identity auction makes sybil attacks uneconomical. To register, an agent must escrow a bond whose price follows a spiral schedule: each active identity in a region raises the minimum bond for the next, so the thousandth clone costs exponentially more than the first. Bonds sit in a shared treasury, an oasis of locked capital that only honest, continuously attested agents can reclaim with interest, like nectar earned through verified participation. Attackers spawning clones must freeze enormous capital forever, since detected identities forfeit bonds to the treasury.
